headline: Explore every trie branch for a wildcard
statement: Implement WordDictionary.addWord(word) and search(word). A query period matches exactly one lowercase letter; all other characters must match themselves. A search must match a whole stored word of the same length. Supply operations and args arrays.
constraints: Added words use lowercase English letters
Search words use lowercase letters or periods
At most two periods in each search
intuition: Store inserted words as letter paths in a trie. A normal search character follows one matching edge. A '.' may follow any letter edge, so keep all possible matching nodes for that step. At the end, accept only a node marked as a complete inserted word.
approach: Insert words as character paths and mark their final nodes.
Start a search frontier at the root; advance by one literal child or all letter children for a period.
After the full query, succeed if any reachable node carries the terminal marker.
correctness: After i query characters, the frontier is exactly all nodes reached by a prefix matching those characters. Literal and wildcard transitions list precisely the permitted next letters. Checking endpoint markers after all characters therefore matches whole words, never merely prefixes.
bruteForce: Store all words and compare every word character-by-character to each query, costing O(WL) per search.

complexity.space: O(total stored prefix characters + 26^d) search frontier
complexity.explanation: d is the number of wildcard periods, at most two; the trie shares common prefixes.

pitfalls: A period consumes exactly one letter.
Do not treat the terminal marker as a wildcard child.
A path alone does not prove a complete word match.
